newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FERGUS LEADS QUAD CITY CLASSIC AFTER TWO ROUNDS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FERGUS LEADS QUAD CITY CLASSIC AFTER TWO ROUNDS.

text.p: Keith Fergus
shot a six-under-par 64 Friday to take a one-shot lead in the
$1.35 million Quad City Classic after two rounds.
Fergus was at nine-under 131 through two rounds, a shot
ahead of former PGA Tour Rookie of the Year Robert Gamez and
veteran Ed Dougherty, both of whom shot five-under 65.
Russ Cochran, David Toms and hometown favourite Sean
McCarty were three shots back.
Playing in just his eighth tournament this year, Fergus
launched his morning round with an eagle on the sixth hole,
the easiest par-5 on the 6,792-yard Oakwood layout, birdied
the short par-4 finishing hole, the tightest drive on the
hole, with a sand wedge to 2 feet and netted four birdies in
between.
"I'm fortunate to be in this position," said Fergus, who
left his job as the University of Houston golf coach for the
Nike Tour in March of 1994 and has played a limited PGA Tour
schedule the last 2-1/2 years. "But I worked hard to be in
this position.
"I am enjoying this again."
Despite winning three tournaments over a three-year
stretch from 1981-1983, Fergus left the tour and took the
coaching job at his alma mater in 1987 after struggling for a
couple of years.
"When I left in 1987, I didn't think I'd ever want to be
back out here," he said. "I had played 10 years and had some
success, but I wasn't enjoying it anymore."
Six years later, he discovered he missed it. "I feel like
this is what I was put on this earth to do."
Gamez, winless since winning twice in his 1990 rookie
season, opened his round with three straight birdies and added
two more on his way in, but was frustrated after failing to
hit four fairway sand-wedge approaches closer than 20 feet and
settling for pars each time.
"I left some shots out there," he said.
Daugherty was six under for his round and tied for the
tournament lead after making back-to-back birdies on his 10th
and 11th holes, but bogeyed twice coming home before
salavaging his seventh birdie of the afternoon on his final
hole to stay within a shot of Fergus.
McCarty, a 24-year-old former University of Iowa golfer
who is making his PGA Tour debut, played in front of a gallery
that included much of his tiny hometown of West Branch, Iowa,
which is located 70 miles (110 km) west of Oakwood.
He eagled his first hole and remained unflappable
throughout a three-under round -- despite hitting a woman in
the head with his drive at the 16th hole.
"I felt bad about that," he said. "I owe her a beer or
something."
A total of 88 players survived the midway cut, which fell
at even-par 140. The survivors included Scott Hoch, the only
member of the tour's top 20 money-winners in the field.
After struggling two days with his putter, Hoch, the
fifth-leading U.S. Ryder Cup point-getter, said he will not
play next week's British Open at Troon, Scotland.
